chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babawayh al-Faqih al-Qummi, the author of this book (may God have mercy on him), said: It was narrated to me by my father (may God have mercy on him), who said: It was narrated to me by Sa'd ibn Abdillah from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Khattab from Safwan ibn Yahya from Ishaq ibn Ghalib from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

A scholar (hibr) from the rabbis of the Children of Israel worshipped Allah until he became like a dry stick. So Allah, the Mighty and Sublime, revealed to the prophet of his time: 'Say to him: By My Might, My Glory, and My Power, even if you worship Me until you melt like a dry stick melts in a pot, I will not accept it from you until you come to Me through the door I have commanded you.'

key_terms.أَحْبَار: Plural of hibr, referring to learned scholars or rabbis
key_terms.الْبَاب: The door, metaphorically referring to the specific path or command of God
key_terms.الْخِلَال: A dry stick or twig, used here as a metaphor for something brittle or consumed or dried out
key_terms.جَبَرُوت: Might/Power, one of the divine attributes mentioned in the revelation
key_terms.حِبْرٌ: A title for a learned scholar or priest, often used for rabbis
key_terms.عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ: The Mighty and Sublime, an honorific for Allah

ai.seo_question: Why did Allah reject the worship of the Israelite scholar despite his intense devotion?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-A'mal* illustrates the Shia principle of *Tawqi'* (divine authorization), where even the most intense devotion is insufficient if it deviates from the specific method prescribed by God or His Prophet. The metaphor of the scholar melting like wax in a pot highlights that God rejects worship performed on human terms rather than divine ones, a concept central to understanding the authority of the Imams in Shia jurisprudence. It serves as a reminder that correct *fiqh* (understanding of divine law) is as crucial as the act of worship itself.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1. Muhammad b. Ali b. al-Hussain b. Musa b. Babawayh al-Faqih al-Qummi the author of this book (rah) who said it was narrated to me by my father (rah) said: it was narrated to me by Sa’d b. Abdillah from Muhammad b. al-Hassan b. Abi al-Khattab from Safwan b. Yahya from Ishaq b. Ghalib from Abi Abdillah (a.s.) who said:

Imam Ja’far Sadiq (a.s.) said that a monk from Bani Israel worshipped Allah so much that he become like a dry stick. Allah, the Mighty and Sublime revealed to His prophet of that time to go and say to him that (Allah says), “By My Greatness, Might and Power, even if you worship Me till you melt like something in the cooking pot, also, I will not accept it from you until you come to Me from the door I have ordered for you.”
